<p align="center">
  <b>CASTAWAY</b> <i>(working title)</i>: ten hours of one tiny island, one tall palm, one raft and one young woman in headphones.<br>
  She idles, nodding to the music. Every so often, something happens. Then she idles some more.<br>
  <sub>The page above takes about eight seconds to arrive at 1200 bit/s. The video takes ten hours. Nobody here is in a hurry.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <kbd>1</kbd>&nbsp;<a href="MUSING.md">the&nbsp;island</a> &nbsp;&nbsp;
  <kbd>2</kbd>&nbsp;<a href="activities.toml">the&nbsp;timetable</a><br>
  <kbd>3</kbd>&nbsp;<a href="tools/make_audio.py">the&nbsp;sound</a> &nbsp;&nbsp;
  <kbd>4</kbd>&nbsp;<a href="tools/serve.py">run&nbsp;it</a>
</p>

A stationary-frame lo-fi video in the spirit of the ten-hour streams, and an unofficial remake inspired by *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver: its small-island routines and visual comedy, repainted as a sunny, hand-painted coastal scene. 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, always daytime. More than 90 activities, most of them on four timers: something everyday every few minutes (a coconut, a sandcastle, a spot of fishing) and, once in a very long while, a walk across the water for an iced coffee. Each one starts on the next bar of the music, so every gag lands on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

Preview it live in the page, then export a YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes frame-exact H.264 with WebCodecs (68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), and the server mixes in the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.

<details>
<summary><kbd>1</kbd> <b>the island</b>: who lives there, and what keeps happening to her</summary>

```text
 1a  THE ISLAND                                    Lagoon Pages   0.00/min
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 RESIDENT     one young woman: brown hair in a low bun, cream headphones,
              coral tank top, cream shorts, bare feet
 FIXTURES     one tall palm, one raft, a great deal of time
 EVERYDAY     coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, a sandcastle (the
              tide takes it)
 BUSHCRAFT    fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear
              fishing, and a kumara planted in the sand that grows all
              video long
 VISITORS     a sea turtle. a stray cat (grey tabby, white chest) on a
              crate, who climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats away
              again, then comes back another time. a shark in headphones,
              nodding to the beat. a tour boat of selfie-takers. a bro on
              an electric hydrofoil: one shaka, then gone
 POST         a bottle that washes straight back. later, a different
              bottle, with a reply. a delivery drone whose parcel is
              another pair of headphones
 SIGNAL       one bar, at the top of the palm
 CRAB         under a falling coconut. then wearing it, and leaving
 EXIT         she could leave any time: she walks out over the water and
              comes back with an iced coffee
 RESCUE       very rarely, she spots a ship and waves like mad. it hoots
              back, and sails on
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 SCENERY      26 entries. shore waves and drifting cloud shadows: built.
              birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins,
              sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko, one rain shower: planned
```

Most of the time, none of that is happening. She is busy about a third of the time and idling the rest, nodding on the beat, which is the point. Notes, decisions and the project's own log live in [MUSING.md](MUSING.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><kbd>2</kbd> <b>the timetable</b>: page 2, with arrivals and departures</summary>

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/53-viewdata-page_opus_5.5-timetable.svg" width="640" alt="Lagoon Pages, page 2: the Castaway timetable on a grey 40-column viewdata screen. Four timers: regular, every 2 to 5 minutes, about 155 per 10 hours; occasional, every 12 to 25 minutes, about 30; rare, every 30 to 60 minutes, about 13; super rare, every 3 to 6 hours, about 2; idle, the other two thirds. Arrivals: turtle, visiting; cat, on a crate; drone: headphones; bottle: a reply; shark, nodding; tour boat, selfies; ship: unnoticed. Departures: bottle (comes back); cat, on a crate; sandcastle, by tide; coconut, with crab; bro, carving off; her (coffee run); ship: unnoticed. Every start waits for the next bar: 3 s. Default run 10:00:00, seed 1992. Keys: BACK page 1, REPEAT ten more hours.">
</p>

[activities.toml](activities.toml) is the whole timetable: every activity, how long it lasts, how often it comes round and what has to be true first. Counts on page 2 are the medians of 200 simulated runs, as the file says at the top; the super-rare timer fires at most 3 times a run, and chained follow-ups (the tide after a sandcastle, a reply after a bottle) come on top.

Each timer picks by weight among the activities that are free right now: off cooldown, their lane clear, their conditions met. She has one lane. The cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, the shore and the kumara patch have their own, so things overlap: a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut, and the ship even waits for her to get busy. Hence the last line in both columns.

`python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates a 10-hour run (the default is 10:00:00 with seed 1992).

</details>

<details>
<summary><kbd>3</kbd> <b>the sound</b>: all of it synthesized, none of it heard yet</summary>

```text
 3a  THE SOUND                                     Lagoon Pages   0.00/min
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 SOURCE       tools/make_audio.py. no samples, no loops, no recordings,
              so no third-party licence applies
 FILES        more than 150, every one of them made by code
 THEME        a seamless 60 s loop: 80 BPM, F major, ii-V-I-vi, 20 bars
              of exactly 3 s. electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums,
              vinyl crackle
 OCEAN        a seamless 60 s loop of its own
 MIX          -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP. levels for the
              master and for each routine
 REVIEWS      none yet. nobody has listened to it
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

The banner keeps the same time. Under the paint, its picture runs on a 60-second loop from the moment it loads: 20 bars of 3 seconds. She nods on every beat, the clouds step one block a beat, the cursor blinks a beat on and a beat off, and every action in the picture starts on a beat or a bar line, the way activities start on the bar in the real schedule. Source: [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py).

</details>

<details>
<summary><kbd>4</kbd> <b>run it</b>: preview, export, check, reel</summary>

```sh
python tools/serve.py              # live preview and MP4 export,
                                   # at http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py           # check the schedule, simulate 10 hours
python tools/render_demo.py --dev  # a reel of every activity, with a HUD
```

[tools/serve.py](tools/serve.py) serves the renderer, [web/index.html](web/index.html): live preview, then a frame-exact MP4 for YouTube (the browser encodes the picture, the server mixes the sound and joins the two). [tools/render_demo.py](tools/render_demo.py) is the older Python reference renderer; its dev reel plays every activity in turn with a heads-up display. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults, which suits a 1200 bit/s terminal very well.

Status: in development. No video has been published yet.

</details>

<details>
<summary><kbd>GUIDE</kbd> how the page above was made</summary>

The banner is one SVG drawn by a dependency-free Node script, with no fonts, no images and nothing fetched: every letter and every block is a rectangle.

- **The page** is 40 columns by 25 rows of 8 by 10 cells, as on a videotex terminal. Row 0 is the status row, empty except the line-state letter on the far right (F for a moment, then C: connected). The title is double size (2 by 2 cells a letter), and the rest is a 5 by 7 dot-matrix face with lower case and descenders.
- **The greys** are the eight videotex colours as a monochrome set shows them, in order of brightness: black, blue, red, magenta, green, cyan, yellow, white.
- **The picture** is mosaic graphics: each cell splits into 2 by 3 blocks (3, 4 and 3 units tall), so the 12 picture rows make 80 by 36 blocks. The island, the palm, her, the raft, the bottle and the ship are all drawn at that resolution.
- **The paint** runs at 1200 bit/s, 120 characters a second, row by row, up to the last used cell of each row: about eight seconds for the page, after which it holds. Each new NOW message retypes itself at the same speed.
- **The life** is CSS keyframes with steps only, no tweening: hard cuts and stepped movement, on a 60-second loop that matches the theme. At the loop point the REPEAT key on the case goes down.
- **Reduced motion** shows the finished page, with her idle and the bottle at her feet.

Honest small print: a real videotex cell holds two colours, and this picture does not enforce that, so a purist will find cells with three. Page 2 holds still. The look is a style reference to the French videotex terminals of the 1980s and British viewdata; no operator, service, short code, terminal brand or real page design is used.

</details>
